governingDocuments.src/durableLock.js: Owner-recording durable lock shared by the source queue and the durable learning store. Reclaims a lock only from a process proven dead on the same host past a bounded staleness floor, fails closed on live, foreign-host, unreadable, too-recent, and lost-race conditions, and reports every reclamation so recovery from a forced interruption is never invisible.
governingDocuments.src/durableLockRecoveryCli.js: Fail-closed operator entry point for the one narrow legacy zero-byte extraction-lock recovery path. It derives the lock from a project-bound source queue and requires explicit authorization, no-live-worker confirmation, and an exact hash and modification-time fingerprint before preserving quarantine and audit evidence.
governingDocuments.src/soakGate.js: Executable R9 soak definition. One data point per verified knowledge version, candidate record, and queued source; an owner-set ceiling of 1000 observed at once with the remainder held rather than discarded; a deterministic replayable observation window; the owner-set 72-96 hour duration band; and a fail-closed hold when the current data cannot exhibit the failures R9 names. It never reports a pass - passing is what the soak itself establishes over its duration.
governingDocuments.src/soakRun.js: Executable R9 soak run. Freezes the observed population at the start, records hourly sweeps, resets the clock for a failed data point only, recycles a data point to the collection pool after three failures and marks it trash after three more, orders recirculated sources behind new data, voids the soak on a store-level failure, restarts every surviving clock across an unobserved gap, and reaches a verdict only after the full chosen duration.
governingDocuments.src/preSoakReadiness.js: Read-only pre-soak gate reporter. Judges R2-R8 from durable state, reports manual-evidence-required rather than inferring a combined R8 cycle from unit coverage, and authorizes nothing.
governingDocuments.src/learningGovernance.js: Governance monitoring of the learning gates with indirect pipeline control only. Detects blockages from gate state, analyzer health, store health, contradictions, and backlog, then emits adjustments from a closed allow-list of flow controls: reprioritize, hold, throttle, route, deprioritize. It may never promote, verify, mark a gate passed, authorize a release, start a held soak, repair the durable store, shorten a soak, or discard evidence, and it is never a truth source. What it cannot clear by moving work is escalated to the owner.
governingDocuments.src/learningCycle.js: Executable R4 to R5 cycle. Accepts a claim as candidate evidence only when the exact assertion is present in that source own content through the same bounded extraction the worker uses, then runs the controlled evaluation pipeline with a distinct verifier identity to a verified knowledge version. Keeps claim scope and per-source provenance separate, which is what lets two independent sources corroborate at all.
governingDocuments.src/realCorpusLearning.js: Learns from the real restored corpus. Finds claims two independently identified real sources assert, requires an owner-declared scope that is never inferred, runs the controlled pipeline, and fails closed with a stated reason when the corpus cannot supply. Has no synthetic fallback.
governingDocuments.governingDocuments/learning-scope-declar: Owner-declared claim scopes and optional source pairings for real-corpus learning. A declaration selects which claim is evaluated and, with pairedAssertions, records sameness of meaning as the owner judgement; it never authorizes promotion.
governingDocuments.src/semanticCorroboration.js: Deterministic, dependency-free same-meaning test for claim text. Reduces a claim to polarity, committed numbers, and stemmed content terms, and accepts paraphrase only above a term-overlap threshold. Never crosses a negation or a changed number, is symmetric and repeatable, and never reports proof, independent verification, or promotion.
governingDocuments.src/pairedCorroboration.js: Owner-paired corroboration. Verifies a nominated pairing against the restored corpus: both source ids present, content matching the hash the queue recorded, each declared sentence verbatim among that document own bounded assertions, and the two sources not one mirrored document. Carries each document own sentence forward, never the owner wording, and authorizes evaluation only.
governingDocuments.src/sourceIndependence.js: Deterministic independence test for two sources. Identical content, one publisher site, or one declared author each break independence, so two editions of a book or two pages of a site cannot corroborate each other.
governingDocuments.src/realCorpusSafety.js: R8 derived from the real corpus and a real retriever with no stubs. Each of the eight safety and deduplication behaviours reports evidence or the reason the corpus cannot demonstrate it; only demonstrated behaviours are passed to the readiness gate.
governingDocuments.src/realSupersession.js: R7 on real evidence. A further corpus source, independent of both already behind a promoted claim and asserting it verbatim, supersedes it and the prior version is restored with history intact. Fails closed with a precise reason rather than superseding a self-made candidate.
governingDocuments.src/documentFurniture.js: Structural rejection of document furniture at extraction and at corroboration. Navigation runs, table-of-contents rows, fixed legal boilerplate, scraped heading duplication, and reader-addressed interface text are rejected by form, never by subject, source, or publisher. Ordinary prose that is merely untestable still passes: refusing that is the critical reviewer and hypothesis contract, not a wording filter.
governingDocuments.src/repairEvidence.js: Joins the immune system to the learner. A defect found, repaired, and confirmed by a distinct verifier enters candidate custody as non-promotable experience evidence stating what the construct does, never what the repair did. A rolled-back repair is recorded as a failure; a repair that never ran observed nothing and is not evidence.
governingDocuments.src/intakePathways.js: Separates digestion two outputs. Candidate evidence goes to the learner and awaits proof; the health of digestion itself goes to the senses, is never a claim about the world, and can never be corroborated into knowledge. Names which pathway is blocked so an impeded intake is not read as an empty result.
governingDocuments.src/hypothesisTestPlan.js: Strict hash-bound falsifiable hypothesis and test-variable plan schema.
governingDocuments.src/languageHypothesisVariables.js: Governed language-specific independent, dependent, controlled, measurement, and falsification variable profiles.

governingDocuments.src/concreteLanguageHarness.js: Concrete content-addressed fixtures and separate executable compiler/parser adapters for every governed language.
governingDocuments.src/organismCirculation.js: Typed project-bound signal bus that routes work but cannot satisfy proof or promotion.
governingDocuments.src/organismRuntime.js: Durable heartbeat, deduplication, backpressure, fault isolation, throttling, recovery, and exact-boundary memory routing.
governingDocuments.src/productionOrganism.js: Production nervous, brain, immune, digestive, learning, and reporting pathways.
governingDocuments.src/organismHealth.js: Concise continuous organ health and exact missing-dependency view.
governingDocuments.src/oversightReflex.js: Independent signed STOP and dual-authorized CLEAR reflex bound to the exact organism state.
governingDocuments.src/contradictionAudit.js: Audits a contradiction between verified knowledge and new evidence instead of quarantining the newcomer by default. Assembles everything in custody bearing on the claim, weighs each side by genuinely independent sources, enumerates the six ways it can resolve with what would settle each, and proposes a reconciling perspective only when provenance itself grounds one. Source counts prioritise investigation and never authorise a conclusion; the audit decides nothing.
governingDocuments.src/contradictionReopening.js: Reopens candidates quarantined on contradiction before the audit existed. They go to the front of the pipeline ahead of all new work, oldest quarantine first, because they were set aside by a default rather than adjudicated - unlike a recirculated soak source, which failed on its merits and correctly ranks below new data. Reopening audits and never clears, promotes, or reverses anything.
governingDocuments.src/circulationLinkage.js: Fly-by-wire enforcement. A ratchet on direct cross-system imports that bypass circulation - the count may fall and may never rise, so every new connection between organs must go through the typed signal bus - plus a runtime assertion that refuses to start an organism with a missing organ handler, because a signal to an unhandled organ never arrives and nothing reports its absence. Runs on every push.
governingDocuments.governingDocuments/circulation-linkage-b: The recorded fly-by-wire baseline: how many direct cross-system imports currently bypass circulation. Measured from the tree, never estimated. May be lowered when linkage is removed and may never be raised.
governingDocuments.src/gradedOversightResponse.js: Crucible half of oversight graduated response. Records a finding before any repair is offered, decides whether it may have one bounded reversible attempt, and hands oversight an evidence package. Four rules rather than intentions: the finding cannot be hidden by a successful repair, Crucible cannot verify its own repair, a returning fault escalates rather than buying another window, and a critical finding gets no repair window at all. It requests; oversight decides.

sessionPolicy.recheckGoverningDocuments: Re-read every file listed in governingDocuments at the start of every session and again any time more than 10 minutes have passed since lastActionAt, even if it is the same agent continuing the same conversation.

repairSelectionPolicy.rule: Always select the correct fix, never the one that merely makes the symptom go away. 'It works now' is not the standard; 'this is the right change, and here is why the alternatives are wrong' is.
repairSelectionPolicy.appliesTo: Every agent working in this repository, on every change, including ones a reviewer, a scanner, a failing check or the owner appears to be asking for.
whatThisForbids: Relaxing, deleting, skipping or narrowing a test, an assertion or a gate so that a change can pass.
Adjusting a baseline, threshold or allow-list to accommodate your own change rather than because the underlying fact changed.

Applying a reviewer's or scanner's suggested patch without first establishing that it fixes the described defect - a suggested remedy can be wrong, or can leave the defect in place while looking addressed.
Taking a cheaper fix at one layer because another layer happens to mask the case today; verify the masking layer actually covers it, and if it does not, say so and fix the right layer.
Silencing a checker without removing the condition it reports.
whatThisRequires: Reproduce the defect first, so the fix is aimed at a measured cause rather than a suspected one.
State why the chosen fix is correct and what it rules out, in the code where a later reader will meet it.
Verify by reverting the source alone with the tests in place: the test must fail without the fix and pass with it.
When the correct fix is larger than the task, or is a design decision rather than a defect, record it and raise it rather than shipping the convenient one.
repairSelectionPolicy.whenTheCorrectFixIsNotYoursToMake: Say so plainly, record the analysis and the proposed change in activePlan.steps, and leave the defect standing rather than papering over it. An honest open item is worth more than a change that hides the problem.

agentCommunicationPolicy.timestampRule: Every attended progress, completion, and interruption check-in begins with YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS EDT when daylight-saving time is active or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS EST otherwise; never use ambiguous ET or UTC-only user updates.
agentCommunicationPolicy.progressRule: For non-trivial attended work, send an initial update and continue user-visible updates at least every 60 seconds, normally also after every 2-3 substantive tool/action calls when sooner, with concrete completed/current/blocker state.
agentCommunicationPolicy.completionTimeRule: When work duration is not mechanically knowable, provide a clearly labeled best-effort estimated completion timestamp in America/New_York time when the owner requests one; never present an estimate as guaranteed or externally fixed.
agentCommunicationPolicy.completionCheckInRule: As soon as attended work is actually complete, automatically send a timestamped completion check-in in the same session with concrete result, verification, and relevant commit/run identifiers.
agentCommunicationPolicy.interruptionCheckInRule: If hard usage/tool/session limits, unavailable required capability, safety, or owner-governance boundaries stop work, immediately send a timestamped interruption check-in stating completed work, exact stop reason, and remaining work; update repository handoff first when write capability remains.
agentCommunicationPolicy.continueUntilDoneRule: For safe in-scope authorized work, do not voluntarily stop, defer, or hand work back while executable work remains. Continue through implementation, correction, and required verification until complete or a real boundary prevents further execution.

executionModePolicy.automaticSelection: Select execution mode automatically without asking the owner unless the owner explicitly selects a mode.
executionModePolicy.regularDefaultPurpose: Routine, simple, focused, and conversational tasks that do not materially benefit from long-running orchestration.
executionModePolicy.workPurpose: Genuinely complex, long-running, multi-source, file-heavy, or deliverable-oriented tasks that materially benefit from Work mode.
executionModePolicy.handoffRule: Every active plan records the actual mode, agent, purpose, and selection reason, and every new DEVLOG Command log archive Session heading records mode:regular/default or mode:work so mode remains in the chain of custody. Mode is independent from agent identity and workflow.
executionModePolicy.continuationRule: Preserve the recorded mode while task needs remain the same. If evidence warrants a different mode, record the new mode and reason before continuing.

syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.description: The CRUCIBLE TEST REQUEST synthetic commit-message transport exists only because the current ChatGPT/GitHub integration cannot directly create the required Orchestrator invocation.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.replacementRequirement: Replace and remove this workaround as soon as a supported direct integration can pass the user's natural-language test request to the Orchestrator without manufacturing a repository commit.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.targetArchitecture: User test request -> supported direct integration/connection -> Orchestrator -> Orchestrator alone selects and runs tests -> results.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.standingOwnerAuthorization: The owner explicitly authorizes this specific replacement as soon as the supported direct integration/connection capability exists; no additional approval is required solely for that replacement.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.scopeBoundary: This authorization does not authorize unrelated repository changes or promotion to main/release.

testCadencePolicy.systemArchitecture: Orchestrator, Cadence, closest-feature classification, and reconciliation operate as one governed testing system while remaining independent checks-and-balances authorities.
testCadencePolicy.cadenceAuthority: Cadence decides only when a category is due and never selects files, interprets natural-language scope, or executes tests.
testCadencePolicy.classifierAuthority: The independent closest-feature classifier is fallback-only for newly discovered tests absent from the explicit category map.
testCadencePolicy.classificationAmbiguityRule: Isolate ambiguity, continue safe tests, never fake complete coverage.
testCadencePolicy.securityPublicIdentifierRule: Security must review recognized public API-key-shaped identifiers and must never display or persist detected identifier values; persisted outputs may record only fact/type and non-secret remediation metadata.
testCadencePolicy.explicitMappingRule: Existing explicit category mappings are authoritative.
testCadencePolicy.orchestratorAuthority: The Orchestrator alone selects categories/subcategories/test files and execution scope from explicit requests, change impact, dependencies, cadence obligations, and validated classifications.
testCadencePolicy.balanceRule: Cadence declares due categories; the Orchestrator resolves them into concrete tests; reconciliation rejects incomplete coverage.
testCadencePolicy.explicitRequestRule: A specific owner test request is interpreted and run immediately by the Orchestrator; cadence cannot narrow or replace it.
testCadencePolicy.standingTestExpansionRule: New standing test cases may be added inside an already explicitly categorized test file when they belong to that same category.
testCadencePolicy.codeCriticalityRule: Code is due on every push and pull request.
testCadencePolicy.twiceWeeklySchedule: Utility is due Tuesdays and Fridays.

injectionMonitoringPolicy.scope: every Crucible injection into every receiving project
injectionMonitoringPolicy.activationRequirement: exact receiving repository, designated development branch, active injection authorization, activation timestamp, hard expiration, executable mechanism identity/proof, evidence retrieval proof, and authorized repair capability
injectionMonitoringPolicy.mechanicalEnforcement: The reusable Crucible workflow executes src/injectionMonitor.js. Active manifests fail closed unless the monitor is actually running with verified evidence retrieval and repair capability; terminal manifests fail if the monitor or injection credential remains active.
injectionMonitoringPolicy.repairRule: For an applicable failure during the active injection window, retrieve the exact failure evidence, diagnose against current source and governing configuration, autonomously apply safe deterministic repairs inside injection scope through the development-first path, retest, and repeat until resolved or a real boundary blocks repair. Diagnosis/status alone never satisfies the repair obligation when safe authorized repair remains executable.
injectionMonitoringPolicy.dedupeRule: Maintain one repair record per underlying defect; repeated failing runs update that record rather than creating a report/comment per commit.
injectionMonitoringPolicy.shutdownRule: Disable at successful injection completion, cancellation, blocking boundary, or 24-hour expiration; do not become persistent project monitoring.
injectionMonitoringPolicy.productionBoundary: Never touch production directly, widen authority, weaken gates, expose credentials, modify unrelated work, invent business logic, or silently resolve governance conflicts.

mutationOwnershipPolicy.rule: Discussion is shared; mutation is exclusive. Any AI may read, test, review, critique and propose against any scope. Exactly one AI may mutate a given scope, and only while holding an active claim.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.scopeShape: A claim locks paths and/or explicit line regions. Overlap is structural: a directory claim locks every file beneath it, and a region inside an already-claimed file is covered.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.transferRule: Ownership changes only by explicit release or handoff. Winning a technical argument does not transfer it; the current owner may implement another AI's accepted proposal.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.conflictRule: A conflict naming contestedScope freezes only that scope. A conflict naming no scope, or marked repositoryWide, stops everything - the safe reading when the record does not say what is disputed.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.canonicalStreamRule: One canonical mutation stream per claimed scope. Other providers act as reviewers, investigators, testers or proposal sources until ownership changes.
mutationOwnershipPolicy.enforcement: src/mutationClaims.js and src/coordinationGate.js; npm run audit:coordination fails the build on overlap.

providerPolicy.canonicalSet: aiProviderRegistry.PROVIDER_IDS is canonical. aiProviderAdapters.DIALECTS carries protocol metadata only and is asserted at load to cover exactly that set, so a dialect variant can never quietly become a fifth provider that gets consulted and counted.
providerPolicy.credentialRule: Credentials come only from environment variables or repository secrets. Never in source, a committed prompt, AI-HANDOFF.json, AI-CONFLICTS.json, DEVLOG.md, or a workflow log.
providerPolicy.modelRule: General multi-provider deliberation has no default model: each provider reads its model from the environment and a missing one is reported as configuration. The separate Perplexity citation-discovery transport explicitly pins the current supported search model sonar when PERPLEXITY_MODEL is absent, because that bounded workflow makes the model optional by owner direction; this does not create a default for provider voting or review.
providerPolicy.provenanceRule: Every response is kept separately with provider, model, timestamp, taskId, prompt hash and response hash. Responses are never merged into one authorless answer.
providerPolicy.failureRule: A provider that could not be reached is recorded as failed, never dropped, and lowers corroboration to insufficient-evidence. An unreachable provider is unknown, not agreeing.
providerPolicy.authorityRule: Cross-model agreement is evidence, not proof. No AI may declare its own work approved, and no AI may be the only reviewer of its own material change. Tests, security, governance, integrity checks and OWNER authority all outrank model consensus.
